newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee motors higher on NY, stock news.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee motors higher on NY, stock news.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures rebounded in the afternoon on firmer New York values but prices finished off their peaks on overhead origin selling, traders said.

In another intresting feature, the spot November's premium to second-position January widened on keen buying amid concerns over near-term coffee supplies. Traders said the late rebound after sleepy morning trading was also seen as a technical correction to Monday's sell-off.
New York arabica prices were moderately firmer but just shy of key resistance toward midday. The market had opened higher, buoyed by an unexpected sharp drawdown in U.S. certified stocks.
The figures released after the market closed on Monday showed a sharp fall of 10,433 60-kg bags on the week to 31,669 bags -- the lowest level in at least 10 years, analysts said.
"The news supported the market quite well," said one trader.
By the finish, November stood $15 higher at $1,503 a tonne after first breaching immediate support at $1,488, then reversing and breaking above resistance at $1,500.
The next key hurdle is seen at $1,520 and support at $1,471.
November's premium to January widened to touch a high of $62 before closing at $58, up from Monday's finish of $49.
The remaining months were $9 to $12 firmer.
Volume on the exchange reached 3,819 lots.
Traders said origin selling was keeping a lid on the upside in London. On the downside, keen roaster interest was seen at the lows.
Traders said the U.S. stock data, coming at the start of the 1996/97 South American harvest, could underpin prices and boost CSCE December's premium to the distant months.
"That should produce more support on the Dec/March switch (in New York) because there is less and less coffee that can be delivered to the market," said one.
"The origins will not have any volume to arrive in the U.S. until at least early December," he said.
